setup: Stand facing a sturdy upright support, such as a squat rack post or suspension trainer handles, with feet roughly shoulder-width apart.
Turn your toes slightly outward to match your natural hip anatomy.
Grasp the support firmly at roughly chest height.
steps: Use your arms for support as you push your hips back and bend your knees to sink down into a deep squat.
Descend until your hips are below your knees while keeping your heels flat on the floor.
Hold the bottom position with a tall, upright chest and relaxed hips.
Maintain the static hold for the target duration, using the support to keep your balance and prevent collapsing.
Pull gently with your arms and drive through your midfoot to stand back up.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply into your belly to encourage your hips and pelvic floor to relax into the bottom position.

common_faults.correction: Widen your stance slightly, turn the toes out more, and lean back into the support to keep the entire foot planted.

common_faults.fault: Excessively rounding the spine into a slouched posture.
common_faults.correction: Pull your chest through your shoulders and maintain a proud, neutral spine using the support.
Actively push your knees outward in line with your middle toes.

precautions: Ensure the anchor or rack is completely stable and will not tip under your body weight.
Do not bounce aggressively at terminal hip or knee flexion.

name: Supported Deep Squat Hold
